claim: ClaudeAgentOptions in the Python Agent SDK carries per-run parameters including max_turns and max_budget_usd (client-side cost estimate cap, which can be exceeded so leave headroom).
quote: Stop the query when the client-side cost estimate reaches this USD value. The estimate can pass this value, so leave headroom .
title: Agent SDK Python reference

claim: Python SDK setting_sources defaults to loading all filesystem settings (CLI defaults); passing [] disables user, project and local settings.
quote: Control which filesystem settings to load. Pass [] to disable user, project, and local settings.
title: Agent SDK Python reference

claim: Structured output in the SDK: pass a JSON Schema via output_format (Python) / outputFormat (TS) and read validated data from the result message's structured_output field.
quote: pass it to query() via the outputFormat option (TypeScript) or output_format option (Python).
title: Agent SDK structured outputs

claim: claude-code-action runs in interactive mode (no prompt input, waits for @claude) or automation mode (prompt input supplied, runs on any event without a mention).
quote: Automation mode : when the workflow provides a prompt input, Claude runs without waiting for a mention, subject only to the checks on who can trigger runs .
title: Claude Code GitHub Actions docs

claim: claude_args passes any CLI argument to the action (example: --max-turns 5 --model ... --mcp-config ...), so SDK/CLI-style parameters are set in workflow YAML.
quote: The claude_args parameter accepts any Claude Code CLI argument :
title: Claude Code GitHub Actions docs

claim: In a scheduled GitHub Actions run with a plain-text prompt, Claude has no shell or GitHub API access until tools are granted; scheduled workflows run only from the default branch and public-repo schedules are disabled after 60 days of inactivity.
quote: GitHub runs scheduled workflows only from the default branch and, in public repositories, disables the schedule after 60 days without repository activity.
title: Claude Code GitHub Actions docs

claim: The action rejects bot actors unless listed in allowed_bots, including scheduled runs attributed to the user who last changed the cron schedule.
quote: This check also applies to scheduled runs, which GitHub attributes to a repository user, usually the one who last changed the workflow’s cron schedule.
title: Claude Code GitHub Actions docs

claim: Documented cost controls for the action: --max-turns in claude_args, workflow timeouts, GitHub concurrency limits; runs consume both Actions minutes and API tokens.
quote: Set workflow-level timeouts to avoid runaway jobs
title: Claude Code GitHub Actions docs

claim: Anthropic compares three scheduling options: Cloud (no machine or open session needed, fresh clone, min interval 1 hour), Desktop (your machine, local files), and /loop (session-scoped, min 1 minute).
quote: Use cloud tasks for work that should run reliably without your machine. Use Desktop tasks when you need access to local files and tools. Use /loop for quick polling during a session.
title: Run prompts on a schedule

claim: /loop takes an optional interval and a prompt (or a skill), e.g. /loop 5m check the deploy; tasks are session-scoped and for scheduling independent of any session one should use cloud or Desktop tasks or GitHub Actions.
quote: For scheduling that survives independently of any session, create a cloud scheduled task , set up a Desktop scheduled task , or use GitHub Actions .
title: Run prompts on a schedule

claim: --bare is recommended for scripted and SDK calls and needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (no subscription login); without it, claude -p loads hooks, MCP servers and CLAUDE.md from the host.
quote: --bare is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for -p in a future release.
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: With --output-format json the payload includes total_cost_usd, so scripted callers can track spend; figures are client-side estimates that can differ from the bill.
quote: so scripted callers can track spend without consulting the usage dashboard
title: Run Claude Code programmatically

claim: Third-party write-ups report claude -p can exit 0 with is_error false even when permissions were denied; check permission_denials in JSON output (secondary, search snippet only).
quote: claude -p returns exit code 0 , "subtype": "success" and "is_error": false even when Claude never touched a file. The only trace is the permission_denials array in the JSON
title: Claude Code Hub tip
